title: Supply Chain Controller (all genders)
description:
Willkommen bei Glow25!

Bei Glow25 verbinden wir Beauty mit Wissenschaft und modernster Technologie – KI gehört bei uns ganz selbstverständlich zum Arbeitsalltag. Als Deutschlands führende Kollagen-Marke begleiten wir Menschen dabei, sich in jeder Lebensphase wohlzufühlen und ihre natürliche Schönheit zu unterstreichen.

Für unser weiteres Wachstum suchen wir Menschen mit Substanz: zuverlässig, motiviert und mit echtem Interesse daran, gemeinsam etwas Bedeutendes aufzubauen. Bei Glow25 triffst du auf ambitionierte Ziele und ein Umfeld, das Eigenverantwortung fördert und Leistung wertschätzt – unabhängig davon, welche Rolle du übernimmst.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Das sind unsere aktuellen Herausforderungen und perspektivischen Ziele:

Als Supply Chain Controller (all genders) baust du ein modernes Controlling für unsere Lieferkette auf und agierst als Business Partner für unser Operations Management Team. Du sorgst für Transparenz in einem Bereich, der für unser Wachstum entscheidend ist, und bringst deine Controlling-Expertise direkt in operative Entscheidungen ein.

In diesem Bereich brauchen wir Deine Unterstützung:

  • Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Vorratsbewertung und entwickelst das Inventory Controlling kontinuierlich weiter.

  • Du baust Transparenz über Bestände, Warenbewegungen und deren finanziellen Einfluss auf.

  • Du analysierst zentrale Supply-Chain- und Operations-KPIs wie Bestände, COGS, Logistikkosten und Forecast Accuracy.

  • Du agierst als Business Partner für Operations, Supply Chain und Procurement und bringst finanzielle Perspektiven in operative Entscheidungen ein.

  • Du unterstützt bei Budgetplanung, Forecasts und der operativen Finanzplanung.

  • Du baust Dashboards, Reportingstrukturen und KPIs auf und entwickelst sie weiter.

  • Du erstellst Business Cases für operative Entscheidungen, zum Beispiel zu Lieferanten, Logistikstrukturen oder Bestandsstrategien.

  • Du identifizierst Kosten- und Working-Capital-Optimierungspotenziale entlang der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette.

Du bringst folgende Erfahrungen mit:

  • Du hast ein Studium der Betriebswirtschaft, Finance, Supply Chain Management, Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder eines vergleichbaren Fachbereichs abgeschlossen.

  • Du bringst mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Controlling, Operations Finance, Supply Chain Analytics oder Consulting mit.

  • Du hast einschlägige Erfahrungen mit Beständen, Kostenstrukturen oder operativen KPIs.

  • Du denkst analytisch, arbeitest datengetrieben und kannst komplexe Zusammenhänge klar und verständlich aufbereiten.

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert und eigenständig und behältst auch in einem dynamischen Umfeld den Überblick.

  • Du hast sehr gute Kenntnisse in Excel oder Google Sheets und bewegst dich sicher in der Welt der Zahlen.

  • Du hast Erfahrung mit BI-Tools wie Power BI oder Tableau oder bist motiviert, dich schnell einzuarbeiten.

  • Du hast idealerweise bereits mit ERP-Systemen oder Finanzsystemen gearbeitet.

  • Du interessierst dich für Datenanalyse, Reporting und die Entwicklung aussagekräftiger KPIs.

Das sind Charakterzüge, die Dich beschreiben:

• Du bist analytisch stark und liebst es, komplexe Zusammenhänge zu durchdringen.
• Du bist ein Teamplayer mit ausgeprägter Kommunikationsstärke.
• Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenverantwortlich und lösungsorientiert.
• Du bist proaktiv und bringst Themen selbstständig voran.
• Du bist flexibel und behältst auch in dynamischen Situationen den Überblick.

Diese Rolle passt eher nicht zu dir, wenn...

  • ...du am liebsten für dich allein arbeitest und wenig Austausch mit anderen Teams suchst. Die Rolle lebt vom laufenden Business Partnering mit Production, Supply Chain und Procurement.

  • ...dir der Einstieg ins Controlling noch fehlt. Wir suchen jemanden mit bereits gefestigter Praxiserfahrung, nicht für eine Einstiegsposition.

  • ...du dich ungern mit Tabellen, Kennzahlen und Datenanalyse beschäftigst. Excel/Google Sheets sind hier tägliches Handwerkszeug.

  • ...du feste Prozesse ohne Weiterentwicklung bevorzugst.

Darauf kannst du dich freuen:

  • Arbeite flexibel, so wie es am besten zu dir passt. Arbeite dann und dort, wo du am produktivsten bist – mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und smarter Zeiterfassung.

  • Glow Card – jeden Monat ein Bonus. 50 € Guthaben monatlich für lokale Anbieter – macht 600 € im Jahr extra für dich.

  • Weiterkommen leicht gemacht. Mit unserer Glowcademy und Lernzeit pro Woche bleibst du immer am Ball.

  • 40 % Mitarbeiterrabatt. Auf das komplette Sortiment – das lohnt sich wirklich.

  • Urlaub, der dir guttut. 30 Tage frei + 1 persönlicher Feiertag + bis zu 10 unbezahlte Tage extra, wenn du mal länger abschalten willst.

  • Gesundheit im Fokus. Wir übernehmen bis zu 600 € im Jahr für Zusatzleistungen – von Brille bis Zahnreinigung.

title: Engineer - Data & Platforms (m/f/d)
description:
Your Role & How we work

As our Engineer - Data & Platforms (m/f/d), you build and run the internal data products that our investment team, Quantitative Research and AI Engineering rely on every day: the pipelines, datasets, APIs and tools that turn a large and growing pool of financial and alternative data into something investors can act on. Our stack is Python, SQL, AWS, and Databricks.

You report to Anton Popov, Director of Engineering. This is a hands-on engineering role: most of your time goes to designing, building, and shipping. The team is small, so you take ownership of real products early, and you get a manager and colleagues invested in your growth into investment and data-platform topics. You work closely with Quantitative Research, AI Engineering, Product & Data, and the investment team, and we treat agentic AI as a default in how we build.

What you will do

  • Build and improve the internal products the investment and research teams use daily: data pipelines, datasets, APIs, and tooling, on top of our lakehouse and orchestration stack.

  • Work directly with the teams you build for: take in their requests, triage and prioritise them, protect the integrity and consistency of the product, and explain features and implementation trade-offs in clear, non-technical language.

  • Design, build, and operate reliable data pipelines, ETLs and integrations that handle complex financial and alternative datasets.

  • Bring and reinforce good engineering habits in the team: automated testing at several levels, CI/CD, pull requests and code review, and clear documentation.

  • Contribute to operational excellence: observability, monitoring, data quality, and secure data handling.

  • Use agentic AI across engineering work (coding, review, testing, debugging, documentation) and help the team push these practices forward.


The experience you bring

  • 3 to 5 years of professional software or data engineering experience, building and operating systems in production.

  • Strong Python and strong SQL, with clean, readable code and a good sense for data modelling.

  • Proven engineering discipline: you write tests (unit, integration, data quality), work with CI/CD, and use pull requests and code review as a matter of course, and you can show how you helped a team adopt them.

  • Clear communication with non-engineers: you can explain what you built, why, and what it will and will not do, and you can say no constructively.

  • Hands-on use of AI across engineering functions, including frontier coding systems such as Claude Code and Codex, as a core part of how you work.

  • Genuine interest in investing, financial markets and data, and the ambition to grow into these topics.

  • Nice to have: Databricks or PySpark; data platform tooling such as orchestration (Airflow, Dagster or similar), lakehouse formats (Parquet, Delta, Iceberg) and AWS; experience with investment, financial or market data; building web frontends or APIs for internal tools; LLM systems in production.


2 reasons why you should not apply

  • You prefer fully specified tickets and no contact with users. Here the people you build for sit next to you, ask for things directly, and expect you to weigh in on what should be built and how.

  • You treat AI tooling as an occasional helper. We expect agentic AI to be a default in how you build, review, test, and ship, every day, not now and then.


Your mindset

Position Overview:

This is a vacancy for a hybrid role with regular visits to our HQ in Tutzing, Germany or Amsterdam, the Netherlands. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender identity. 

We are building out the cloud services around the Lobster Data Platform, and we are looking for a Full Stack Software Engineer to join us. What you would build sits between the platform and the people who run it: dashboards that show what is actually happening in a customer's integrations, control planes for provisioning and configuration, self-service tooling that takes routine work off our operations team, and the monitoring around all of it. Python and its API on the backend, Angular on the front end, and you would work on both sides. 

What our customers see is the software you create, so we care as much about how you think about our users as about how you code. The best ideas here tend to come from engineers who ask what someone is trying to achieve and then make that easier. You will have the freedom to bring those ideas to Product Management and to build them. 

Ready to make an impact? 


You’ll get to take ownership of:

  • Developing our Python backend as a product: data model, business logic, validation, migrations, automated tests.
  • Designing and maintaining the RESTful API on top of it, so that services, front-ends and neighbouring systems communicate cleanly.
  • Defining and implementing scalable microservices, from the schema through to deployment.
  • Building the Angular front-end that sits on that API, together with a colleague from the team: components, state, routing and the tests that go with them.
  • Operating and maintaining what you build: containerized, stateless services on AWS, deployed through CI/CD rather than by hand, with monitoring and alerting that tells you something before a customer does.
  • Keeping the running system healthy over time, from dependency and version upgrades to cost and configuration.
  • Evaluating and selecting the tools and technologies that fit a given engineering problem
  • Working closely with Product Management on what the software should do: bringing your own ideas about what customers need, where their work is still harder than it has to be, and how a step could be made simpler.
  • Improving the practices around all of this, from pipelines to test coverage to how we handle incidents.
None of the following is a hard requirement. The more of it you bring, the sooner you can take on that part of the role, and the rest you can pick up here: 
  • A DevOps mindset in practice: you have looked after services you wrote, not handed them over the wall.
  • AWS experience beyond a certification: compute, networking, storage and identity, and a sense of what a design decision costs.
  • Serverless patterns alongside long-running services, and a view on when each one is the right choice.
  • Infrastructure as Code with Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • CI/CD with GitHub Actions or something comparable.
  • Monitoring, logging and alerting: you have set these up rather than only read the dashboards.


We’d love to meet someone with:

  • Around three to five years of professional software engineering with Python as your primary language, and experience running what you built in production.
  • Python craft: strictly typed, well-structured application code. You have built and maintained a backend and its API, not scripts and notebooks, and you model your data at every boundary with Pydantic or something similar.
  • Experience with a web framework such as FastAPI, and with relational databases: schema design, an ORM like SQLAlchemy, and migrations you can run without holding your breath
  • Practical async Python: you have built services on asyncio and you know why a single blocking call inside a coroutine stalls everything around it.
  • Angular and TypeScript on the front end. You can build new components where the product needs them, not only adjust what is already there.
  • A production mindset (you build it, you run it). You think about pipelines, maintainability, testing, telemetry and debugging, and you are willing to be part of working out why something broke
  • A feel for what goes wrong across a network boundary: timeouts, bounded retries with backoff, idempotency.
  • Working knowledge of Docker and of building services that hold no state of their own
  • An eye for the people on the other side of the screen. You ask what a customer is actually trying to get done, and you would rather remove a step than document it.
  • A creative, independent way of working. You are given a goal and room to find the route, and you enjoy filling in the parts that nobody has specified yet.
  • A natural instinct for security. Our software handles customer data and customer environments, so you think about access, secrets and validation while you write, not afterwards.
  • Strong communication skills in English. German is desirable, but not a requirement.


You can look forward to:

  • Opportunity to work flexibly from home 
  • Modern offices in Germany and the Netherlands
  • A personal Learning & Development budget 
  • Up to 30 days of remote work per year from any EU country 
  • Company Pension plan 
  • 30 vacation days a year 
  • 2 additional paid days off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve
  • Location-specific benefits packages (your recruiter will be happy to provide more details during your first chat) 
  • Company-sponsored business travel

For this role, we are open to working with specialists based in Germany or the Netherlands. Whether you prefer working on-site at our offices in Tutzing, Amsterdam, or remotely from a location within one of these countries, we’re happy to accommodate your preferred working style. 
 
If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply!
